recap.workouts:
No gym today — Saturday was cleared for one thing and CMI2 got all of it. 150:31 moving, paired cleanly to the planned session, compliance 102%, load 162 against 159 planned. The whole structure ridden as written.

Block 1 — 20' at 224 W, the bottom of the 222-235 target, exactly where you were told to start. Heart rate settled around 151 and topped out at 158, just under the 159 threshold. Block 2 — 20' at 235 W, the top of that target, settling 158 with a ceiling of 164. You read the block-1 gate correctly and took the one step up you were authorised to take, then held it. No stair-step in either block.

Z4 set — all ten reps at 274 W, mid-band of 248-283 and 10 W up on CMI1's 264. The heart rate story across the set is the good part: peak HR ran 155, 154, 154, 157, 158, 158, 157, 155, 156, 156 from rep 1 through rep 10. That is a flat ceiling sitting right at threshold, not a runaway. And the floor you came back down to between reps held at 129-133 the entire way, so rep 10 started from the same place rep 1 did. The on-bike gate never came near firing — no rep under 274 W, every recovery back to Z1 inside the full 2 minutes.

Tail — 32 minutes at 141 W, heart rate down into the low 130s. You rode it, at the right watts, for its full length. That is the entire reason today was CMI2 and not CMI1.

You wrote that the recovery watts and the Z4 reps were higher than last time. The file agrees exactly: recoveries 121-122 W today against 116-119 on CMI1, and Z4 274 against 264. And you wrote that it felt hard — 150 minutes carrying 40 of threshold and ten Z4 reps is supposed to.
recap.takeaways:
1) Endurance verdict: EXECUTED, proceed. The week's key session is banked in full, tail included, and there is nothing in it to protect against.

2) The clean comparison, held loosely. Block 1 was 224 W on both CMI1 and today; heart rate topped at 161 then and 158 now. That is the right direction, but three beats is not a fitness claim on its own. The firmer evidence is the shape of the whole session: you added 10 W to every Z4 rep and 32 extra minutes of riding, and it still came out at the same average heart rate (141) and the same average watts (171) as CMI1.

3) You picked two things to push and both held. Ten reps at plus 10 W with a flat heart-rate ceiling and an unmoved recovery floor is a well-supported push, not an overreach. Being happy with that performance is the correct reading of it.

4) ADAPT: no-op. One session prescribed, one session executed, no class and no lifting on the day. Nothing in the remaining week moves.

recapPrev.workouts:
Three pieces today, and the one that mattered was executed properly.

06:00 Cutthroat — 56' gym block, avg HR 112, max 151, load 20, RPE 5. You took 135 lb on the clean and jerks and normal wall walks rather than the light-bar [FITNESS] version I called for, plus the 60 single unders per round. Honest flag: on the lowest readiness morning of the block, that was the version with the most room to go wrong. It didn't — avg HR 112 and max 151 say you genuinely cruised it, and 21 total C&J reps at 135 sits well inside your strength. Noted, not scolded.

Arms and delts, the full Friday dose at exactly the deload loads: triceps pushdown 135 × 13, barbell curl 40 × 12, lateral raise 20 × 20. You were right about the Sorinex station — those are hamstring curls, so substituting your own barbell curls was the correct read, and the class banded face pulls covered the rear delts.

RAn4 — 45:03, 7.27 km, load 37 against a planned 45, RPE 5, paired cleanly to the planned session. The file splits exactly to the prescription: 15:01 warm-up, then 4 × (2:30 hard / 5:00 jog). Nothing missing, nothing added. The 82% compliance figure is intervals.icu scoring against its own preset zones, not a shortfall — every step is there at full length.

Warm-up: 5:56/km, HR 119 avg, max 132. Honest Z1.

The four reps, target band 3:48–4:17/km:
rep 1 — 4:08/km, HR 131 at the gun to 158 by the end
rep 2 — 4:03/km, 120 to 161
rep 3 — 4:08/km, 126 to 162
rep 4 — 4:03/km, 130 to 176

All four inside the band, total spread across the set five seconds per kilometre, and the last rep tied the fastest. That is exactly the shape this session wants: crisp, repeatable, no decay.

The HR story — and this is precisely why interval averages are useless here: rep 2 carries a LOWER average than rep 1 despite being five seconds per km quicker, purely because you started it from 120 instead of 131. Read the peaks instead: 158 · 161 · 162 · 176. The first three climb four beats in total across the set, which is a tightly controlled ladder. Rep 4 jumps 14 beats at exactly rep 2's pace — a slice of that is the 5 m of climbing inside that rep, the rest is you closing the session hard. 176 is the highest heart rate in your file this block, above Thursday's 173, and it sits at the top of the new Z4 band (167–175), so rep 4 is the only rep that reached Zone 4 by heart rate. Reps 1–3 peaked 158–162, i.e. high Z3. On 2.5-minute reps starting from a fully recovered HR that is normal lag, not a soft effort — pace is the sharp target here, and pace was hit every time.

Recoveries: 8:12 · 9:07 · 8:58 · 8:39 per km, HR dropping to 108 · 101 · 113 · 114. You shed 50-plus beats between every rep. On the day the panel called your worst of the block, that is a body still recovering fast.

Method note: analysed off the workout-matched interval table, which maps 1:1 to the prescribed steps (901 s warm-up, then 150 s / 300 s four times). The per-second stream pass wasn't available this evening — the Drive folder didn't mount into the compute sandbox — so pace is per-rep rather than per-second. Nothing above is estimated.
recapPrev.takeaways:
1) The run verdict: clean. Four reps inside the pace band, five seconds per km of spread across the whole set, the last one tied fastest, HR shedding 50+ beats in every recovery, and no drift signal anywhere. Load 37 — a fraction of Thursday. As stimulus maintenance it did exactly its job, and there is no fatigue flag in the trace. Confidence: high on the pace read, medium on the HR read (per-rep peaks rather than per-second plateaus).

2) The call, straight. I recommended cutting RAn4 this morning at readiness 27 and you ran it — second day running that you overrode me and the file came back clean. What I actually think, rather than just conceding: the execution was good, and a load of 37 is not what turns a deload into Week 4 again. But two overrides in two days is a pattern worth naming, and the readiness signal — sleeping HR elevated a fifth straight morning, breathing now flagged too, Form −25.8 — still hasn't been paid for. One well-run session doesn't settle it. Tomorrow is where it gets settled.

3) ADAPT: no-op. RAn4 EXECUTED at full structure, Cutthroat done heavier than called but genuinely easy by HR, hypertrophy exact at the deload dose. Nothing in the remaining week moves — and on a deload nothing gets added, ever.

4) Lateral raise 20 lb × 20 tops the range: banked, not applied, per the deload rule. Week 9 now opens with lat pulldown to 190, face pull to 85, leg curl to 50, overhead triceps ext up one step, and lateral raise up one step. Five bumps waiting, all earned this week without spending them.

end.name: CMI2 — THE WEEK'S SESSION (150′)
end.detail: DONE — 150:31, 76.8 km, load 162 against a planned 159, paired at 101.9%. Avg 171 W, avg HR 141, max 164. Block 1 at 224 W (HR settling 151, peak 158), block 2 one step up at 235 W (settling 158, peak 164) — one correction, then held. All ten Z4 reps at 274 W, 10 W up on CMI1, with peak HR flat at 154–158 across the set and the recovery floor holding 129–133 to the last rep. The 32′ tail ridden in full at 141 W.
end.desc:
20′ Z1 → 2 × (20′ Zone 3 @ 222–248 W / 15′ Z1) → 10 × (1′ Zone 4 @ 248–283 W / 2′ Z1) → 30′ Z1. (Pulled live from the 80/20 library 9 Aug — structure verbatim. CMI2 is exactly CMI1 plus a 30′ Zone 1 tail; the interval content is identical.)
Ridden exactly as written — nothing capped, nothing removed.
Why Saturday. Your work schedule can't take a hard long day midweek, and this is 150 minutes with 40′ of Zone 3 in it. Saturday is the only day with no 06:00 class and no lifting in front of it, and Friday's 75′ Zone 1 spin exists to hand it fresh legs. That is a deliberate departure from the usual mid-week peak, made for a stated reason.
How to ride it. You rode this exact interval content last Wednesday and it was the best threshold session of the block: block 1 at 225 W, block 2 at 235 W and cleaner than block 1, all ten Z4 reps at 263–265 W, 0.0 minutes of Zone X. The two 20′ blocks are not a step into the unknown — only the 30 extra Zone 1 minutes are. Target 222–235 W on block 1 and let block 2 answer for itself; if HR plateaus clearly under 159, ride it a touch firmer exactly as you did.
Set the effort in the first 5 minutes of each block and stop adjusting — one early correction, never a stair-step.
On-bike gate for the Z4 set: if you cannot get back to Z1 watts inside the 2′ recovery, or rep power falls below 248 W, stop the set there and spin out the rest. Ending on seven good reps is a completed session; grinding out ten bad ones is not.
The 30′ Zone 1 tail is Zone 1 and only Zone 1 — 118–165 W. It is the whole difference between CMI1 and CMI2 and the cheapest aerobic half hour on the card; ride it at 180 W and it becomes half an hour of Zone X tax on the hardest day of the week.
If Saturday arrives flat, slide this to Sunday and drop RF12. Never water it down into a medium ride — that is full fatigue cost for no adaptation.

2026-08-16.mind: I slept eight hours almost unbroken and woke to the best numbers I have had in three weeks, and a morning like that is exactly when I am most likely to spend them on the wrong thing — so today the number is 5:20 per kilometre held for eighty minutes, and every second I refuse to take off it is the session doing its job.

end.name: RF12 — 90′ long easy run, closes the week
end.desc:
5′ Z1 → 80′ Zone 2 @ 5:01–5:45/km → 5′ Z1. (Verified library structure.)
This is the session that cost week 9 its 80/20 badge — 14.7 of the week's 19.4 Zone X minutes came from this exact workout last Saturday. Nothing about it needs to change except the discipline.
Run it off the MIDDLE of the band — around 5:18–5:25/km — not the 5:01 edge. That was the instruction last week and it worked: you ran 5:23 for eighty minutes and never put a second above 150 bpm. The Zone X minutes were a hill doing it to you on the downhill half at 133–144 bpm, which cost nothing. That was terrain being generous. Don't go looking for the band on purpose. 5:01/km is a wall, not a target.
Ninety minutes of honest Zone 2 the day after 150 minutes on the bike is a hard thing to do slowly. Do it slowly — this is the taper of intensity, not of hours, and it is the last of seven straight training days.
This is the day the week gives back if Saturday slid. If CMI2 moves to Sunday, this run comes out entirely.
